title: Data Free Training of Diffusion Models for Lattice Field Theories
why_read: A clever physics-ML result showing diffusion models can be trained without ground-truth samples by bootstrapping off their own generated data, which could meaningfully reduce the cost of simulating lattice field theories.
analysis: Sampling valid field configurations in lattice field theory is normally very expensive, and training a generative model to do it faster usually requires already having good samples, a circular problem. This paper shows diffusion models can instead be trained using only the known unnormalized probability density of the target distribution, bootstrapping from the model's own generated samples via a 'target score identity.' They test this in a standard toy model (2D phi^4 theory) across different physical phases and get performance comparable to training on expensive traditional Monte Carlo data. This is a solid, if niche, contribution to the growing intersection of generative ML and computational physics.
